transcript: Last night, I saw The Who’s Tommy on Broadway. Now, this is a revival, but I'd never seen any production of it before and didn't really know anything about it going in — I wasn't even very familiar with any of the music. I thought this production was really cool. Sleek and futuristic, but very theatrical. Tommy is a rock opera. The story is told largely through just the music and the staging, and there's pretty much no dialogue. I honestly didn't really find the plot very enjoyable or interesting but the show overall was very exciting. I wasn't emotionally moved but the choreography was thrilling and the way it aligns with the lighting and projections is at many moments mesmerizing. There's a ton of ensemble work here which is really well done. The vocal performances were great as well, but I think they can work on the balance a little more as I felt some of the words were a little muddy. But then again, I suppose a lot of the folks coming in will know the music already. One other sonic observation was that it's quite loud — but it's rock music so I think it kinda has to be. There are some gunshots that I thought were a little unnecessarily loud though, so just be aware. Overall this production was quite good and unlike pretty much everything else on Broadway right now so I give it a warm welcome. With that, another playbill for my collection.
